title: Linux Daily Admin Tasks
description: Learn to think like an administrator: daily checks, storage and LVM, services, networking, access, patching and recovery with guided practice and interview drills.
baseline: RHEL 9 or AlmaLinux 9 · Bash · VMware practice VM · local self-verified exercises
prerequisite: New to Linux? Start Here shows where to open Terminal and how to paste commands. Work in order, read your actual result, and pause at a failed check. You do not need prior server experience.
supplies: Your own disposable RHEL 9 or AlmaLinux 9 VM in VMware Workstation Pro; GNOME is optional. Use NAT for initial downloads.
An authorized sudo account, console access and a pre-lab snapshot. Use a separate new 2 GB virtual disk only for LVM; never initialize the OS disk.
Allow roughly 2 GB VM memory for command-line practice, more for GNOME. Keep host free space for the existing VM, package updates, snapshots and the optional lab disk.
Screens are clearly labeled terminal mockups, not captures from your VM. Commands run only when you paste them into your own terminal. Progress is saved in this browser, not a live account database.

steps.where: Your practice RHEL 9 or AlmaLinux 9 VM · Bash terminal
actions: Read rows by mount point. / is the main filesystem; /boot may be separate.

guide.what: Check capacity, memory and CPU count.
guide.why: A server can run out of bytes, file slots or memory. They need different fixes.
guide.verify: Record the busiest mount and its percentage, available memory and CPU count.
guide.failure: High used memory alone is not proof of trouble: Linux uses cache. Look at available and workload symptoms.

steps.title: Create a tiny file held open by one process
steps.where: Your practice RHEL 9 or AlmaLinux 9 VM · Bash terminal
actions: Use this practice path only. & starts a background job so your prompt returns.
Save the PID immediately; $! means the most recently started background process.
steps.command:
mkdir -p "$HOME/sonic-admin/practice/deleted"
bash -c 'exec 3>"$HOME/sonic-admin/practice/deleted/held.log"; dd if=/dev/zero bs=1M count=8 status=none >&3; sleep 600' &
echo $! > "$HOME/sonic-admin/practice/deleted/holder.pid"
cat "$HOME/sonic-admin/practice/deleted/holder.pid"
steps.expected: A process ID number. The background process holds an 8 MiB practice file for up to 10 minutes.

guide.what: Create a tiny file held open by one process.
guide.why: A process is a running program. A file descriptor is its open connection to a file.
guide.verify: Run the remaining steps in the same terminal within 10 minutes.
guide.failure: If the process has already ended, repeat this setup once. Do not create many holders.
